faqs.question: Are electric vehicles cheaper to own than petrol vehicles?
faqs.answer: Yes, electric vehicles are significantly cheaper to own over their lifetime. While the initial purchase price may be higher, EVs have much lower running costs - electricity costs about 1-2 per km compared to 7-10 per km for petrol. Maintenance costs are also 40-60% lower as EVs have fewer moving parts and don't require oil changes, filter replacements, or clutch maintenance. Most EV owners recover the price premium within 3-4 years through fuel and maintenance savings.

faqs.question: What is the real-world range of an electric vehicle?
faqs.answer: The real-world range of an electric vehicle depends on several factors including driving style, speed, terrain, weather, and use of AC/heating. On average, expect 70-85% of the claimed range in city driving and 60-75% on highways. For example, an EV with a claimed range of 300 km will typically deliver 210-255 km in city conditions and 180-225 km on highways. Cold weather can reduce range by 15-30% due to battery chemistry and heating requirements.

faqs.question: Can I charge an electric vehicle at home?
faqs.answer: Yes, most electric vehicles can be charged at home using a standard 15A plug point. Home charging is the most convenient and cost-effective way to charge your EV. You can simply plug in overnight and wake up to a fully charged vehicle. The charging time depends on your battery size and charger type - a standard 3.3kW charger takes 8-12 hours for a full charge, while a 7.4kW home charger can do it in 4-6 hours.

faqs.question: Do I need a fast charger at home?
faqs.answer: No, a fast charger is not necessary for home use. Most EV owners charge overnight using a standard home charger (3.3kW or 7.4kW), which is sufficient for daily commuting needs. DC fast chargers are primarily designed for public charging stations and highway rest stops where quick top-ups are needed. Installing a home fast charger (22kW+) requires a 3-phase power connection and is not cost-effective for most users.

faqs.question: Are electric vehicles safe to drive in rain and waterlogged conditions?
faqs.answer: Yes, modern electric vehicles are designed to be completely safe in rain and waterlogged conditions. All EV components are sealed and waterproofed to IP67 or higher standards. The battery pack is specially sealed to prevent water ingress. In fact, EVs are safer than petrol cars in waterlogged areas as there's no risk of engine stalling or fuel contamination. However, it's advisable to avoid deep water wading beyond the manufacturer's specified limit (usually 300-500mm).

faqs.question: Are electric vehicle batteries safe?
faqs.answer: Yes, electric vehicle batteries are extremely safe when manufactured by reputable companies. Modern EV batteries come with multiple safety features including thermal management systems, battery management systems (BMS), crash protection, and fire-retardant materials. The probability of EV battery fires is significantly lower than petrol vehicle fires. Leading manufacturers offer 8-year or 1,60,000 km battery warranty, demonstrating their confidence in battery safety and longevity.

faqs.question: What should I check before buying an electric vehicle for the first time?
faqs.answer: Before buying your first electric vehicle, consider these key factors: 1) Daily commute distance - ensure the EV range covers your needs with buffer. 2) Charging infrastructure - check availability of chargers at home, work, and en route. 3) Total cost of ownership - calculate fuel savings vs higher purchase price. 4) Battery warranty - look for at least 8-year warranty. 5) Service network - ensure authorized service centers are accessible. 6) Resale value - research brand reputation and depreciation rates. 7) Features - check for fast charging capability, connected features, and safety equipment.
